raw_action:
import pyautogui, time

# Click on the ruler near the right margin to add a tab stop
pyautogui.moveTo(1600, 220, duration=0.2)
pyautogui.click()
time.sleep(0.5)

# Double-click the new tab marker to open the tab-stop dialog
pyautogui.doubleClick()
time.sleep(0.5)

# In the Tabs dialog, switch alignment to Right and confirm
# (Assuming the 'Alignment' dropdown is focused by default)
pyautogui.press('right')  # Move to 'Right' option
pyautogui.press('enter')
time.sleep(0.5)

# Click OK to close the dialog
# Approximate position of OK button in Tabs dialog
pyautogui.moveTo(950, 550, duration=0.2)
pyautogui.click()

legibility_report.target_element: OK button in the Tabs dialog
legibility_report.why_needed_for_user_goal: To confirm and apply the right-aligned tab stop setting so that the first three words of each line remain left-aligned and the rest of the text can be pushed to the right margin.
legibility_report.expected_visible_effect_next: The Tabs dialog will close and you will see a right-aligned tab marker appear on the ruler at the chosen position near the right margin.
legibility_report.what_could_go_wrong: If the click misses the OK button, the dialog will stay open and the tab stop won’t be applied. Clicking in the wrong spot could trigger an unintended control.

reviewer_result.primary_reason: The proposed click targets a likely dialog OK button, but the dialog itself is not visible and the action is ambiguous enough to risk unintended input or misclicking in the document window.
